reasoning_traces.think:
The Attrition Edge primitive models a causal chain initiated by injury availability, propagating through unit rotation depth changes to affect snap share and pressure distribution. This manifests as a shift in the opponent’s strategic leverage. Snap Share Shift captures the direct consequence of such attrition—whereby a questioned or injured player's reduced presence alters the distribution of snaps and thus the pressure dynamics. Player Efficiency Adjustment introduces a real-time correction mechanism using NGS data, specifically RYOE and stacked box percentages, to refine projections dynamically. These primitives form a dual framework: one rooted in structural attrition (injury → rotation → snap), the other in empirical efficiency (mechanics → performance). The failure mode occurs when injury data is outdated or when NGS metrics misrepresent actual field behavior due to environmental or contextual factors.
